text: The Ratcatcher, Otis Flannegan, is a character in American comic books and other media published by DC Comics, primarily known as an enemy of Batman and part of the Dark Knight's rogues gallery. Once a rat-catcher in the Gotham City Sanitation Department, Flannegan turned to a life of crime after stabbing a man to death in a street fight, leading to a ten-year sentence at Gotham State Penitentiary. After his release, he kidnapped the officials who arrested him and tortured them using his trained rats. Following five years in captivity, one of his prisoners escaped; though Flannegan ordered his rats to kill him, the prisoner reached the surface, where Batman discovered his body, tracked him down, and defeated him by dispersing his rats. After being re-incarcerated, Flannegan escaped his parole hearing by using a flute he carved to control rats through a high-pitched frequency, but was captured again by Dick Grayson disguised as Batman. In Infinite Crisis, Flannegan is revealed to be an OMAC before being killed by a civilian. In the The New 52 continuity reboot, he is resurrected and makes a minor appearance in Batman Eternal. The Ratcatcher has the ability to communicate with and control an army of rats, possesses in-depth knowledge of Gotham City's sewer system and Blackgate Penitentiary's layout, and wields a gas gun capable of manipulating objects with cyanide gas. A female version of the character, Cleo Cazo / Ratcatcher 2, appears in the DC Extended Universe film The Suicide Squad (2021), portrayed by Daniela Melchior. She is the daughter of an unnamed previous Ratcatcher (portrayed by Taika Waititi), who was originally from Portugal and died from a heroin overdose. Cazo moved to America and used her father's equipment to become a criminal, eventually being arrested for armed bank robbery and incarcerated in Belle Reve Penitentiary. Later, she joined the eponymous squad to infiltrate and destroy Jötenheim, a Corto Maltesean laboratory containing the alien Starro, forming bonds with teammates Bloodsport and King Shark, despite Bloodsport's fear of rats. Her pet rat, Sebastian, has vocal effects provided by Dee Bradley Baker. The Ratcatcher first appeared in Detective Comics #585 (April 1988) and was created by writers Alan Grant and John Wagner and artist Norm Breyfogle.
